parts.title: The Rise And Fall Of Detective Stories
parts.article:
(A) The detective story is normally said to have begun in the fertile brain of the great American writer Edgar Allan Poe (1809–49), especially in his stories featuring the detective C. Auguste Dupin. From 1859, Dupin had a counterpart in Monsieur Lecoq, created by the French author Emile Gaboriau. Despite these American and French origins, it was to Britain that detective fiction migrated, where it took root and flourished, becoming a characteristically British genre.

(B) This transition occurred because of one author and his great detective. The most famous of all fictional detectives, Sherlock Holmes, was introduced by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle in A Study in Scarlet, first published in 1887, and later became the subject of four novels and 56 short stories. Nearly all of the Holmes stories are narrated by his friend Dr Watson. Watson is constantly amazed and stupefied by Holmes’s genius, but despite years of working with him, Watson is never able to produce these brilliant insights himself. Holmes is memorably eccentric, with a range of endearing and less endearing habits. He is a brilliant private detective, categorically better than the plodding and mediocre officials of Scotland Yard, who constantly turn to him when they are baffled. This in itself is pure fiction: in real life there were never any brilliant private detectives to whom Scotland Yard turned when they failed, and the Yard’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) had a remarkable clear-up rate and was highly competent.

(C) Most of the Holmes stories are set among the higher levels of 19th-century British society, a world inhabited by professional men, retired army officers and country gentlemen, as well as members of royalty and cabinet ministers. Few take place among the working classes or the very poor, whereas in fact much crime was a product of the poverty and gangs in London’s underworld.

(D) In the 20th century detective stories became increasingly popular. Reading these stories was one of the characteristic aspects of the British middle classes in the ‘golden age’ of British detective fiction—the 1920s and 30s. Their emphasis on rationality, the inevitable triumph of justice, and the existence of an unofficial super-detective tells us much about the society of the time. So, too, do the stock characters and unstated prejudices in these works: country folk and domestic servants were almost always depicted as unintelligent, and women were often depicted in a simplistic, two-dimensional way, although a few female detective writers would present female characters in a more realistic manner.

(E) Most of the well-known British authors of ‘golden age’ detective stories were drawn from the middle classes, like their audience. Conan Doyle was a doctor who turned to writing fiction while he awaited his patients; Freeman Wills Crofts was a railway engineer in Northern Ireland; Gilbert Keith Chesterton and Anthony Berkeley were journalists; Cecil Street a career army officer. Apart from a few superstars such as Agatha Christie, financial rewards for these interwar authors were rather meagre; a few hundred pounds per book—a useful income, but nothing princely.

(F) US writers such as Rex Stout and Ellery Queen attempted to recreate the ‘golden age’ of British detective fiction. For the most part their books were mere imitations of the British models, although they were seldom wholly successful. But in the 1920s and 1930s, America also saw the rise of the ‘hard-boiled’ genre and its detective type: the tough private cop who appeared in the works of Dashiell Hammett and Raymond Chandler. Apart from the violence that appeared throughout their works, Hammett’s and Chandler’s novels were often marked by a political agenda that sought to expose the inequality they saw at the heart of American life. Britain had no real parallel either to their outlook on the world or (until much later) to their violence, but upheld the belief that the authorities should punish criminals regardless of their circumstances.

(G) By around 1960, the classic British detective story was in serious decline. It seemed that writers had simply run out of ingenious plots and puzzles for their detectives to solve. The best-known crime fiction writers, such as P. D. James, eschewed private detectives for police inspectors, and straightforward puzzles for stories that were full of unexpected twists.

(H) Today the detective story no longer exists in Britain, at least in its old form. Arguably this mirrors the transformation of that society as a whole. The belief that scientific developments were invariably beneficial possibly reached its height during the period when the classic detective story flourished, as did the belief in putting rationality at the heart of Britain’s education system. And finally, the central belief that evil-doers would inevitably get their just deserts through the incorruptibility of the judicial system was replaced by a questioning of some of the procedures and decisions associated with that system.

Do the following statements agree with the information given in Reading Passage 1?
In boxes 1–8 on your answer sheet, write.

Q1 C. Auguste Dupin and Émile Gaboriau were both writers of detective stories.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q2 It was Conan Doyle’s creation of Sherlock Holmes that made the detective story a typically British genre.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q3 The positive qualities of the character of Sherlock Holmes outweigh the negative qualities.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q4 Officials at Scotland Yard were unhappy at the way they were portrayed in the Sherlock Holmes stories.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q5 Sherlock Holmes is based on a real private detective who was consulted by Scotland Yard.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q6 Conan Doyle’s work fails to reflect the reality of crime in 19th-century Britain.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q7 In the 1920s and 1930s, most writers of detective stories started to include interesting female characters in their work.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q8 Agatha Christie only earned a few hundred pounds for her books.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

reference:
Q1

解析 原文明确说Dupin是小说里的侦探角色，而Émile Gaboriau是法国作家，并不是两个都是作家。

干扰 你可能看到这两个名字连在一起就觉得他们身份一样，但仔细看原文明说Dupin是侦探角色（the detective）。

句子 (A) The detective story is normally said to have begun in the fertile brain of the great American writer Edgar Allan Poe (1809–49), especially in his stories featuring the detective C. Auguste Dupin. From 1859, Dupin had a counterpart in Monsieur Lecoq, created by the French author Emile Gaboriau.

Q2

解析 原文说侦探小说变成英国特色类型，正是因为柯南·道尔创造了伟大的侦探夏洛克·福尔摩斯。

干扰 你可能没把第三句的“过渡到英国（a characteristically British genre）”和第四五句的“柯南道尔和福尔摩斯”联系起来。

句子 Despite these American and French origins, it was to Britain that detective fiction migrated, where it took root and flourished, becoming a characteristically British genre. (B) This transition occurred because of one author and his great detective. The most famous of all fictional detectives, Sherlock Holmes, was introduced by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle in A Study in Scarlet, first published in 1887, and later became the subject of four novels and 56 short stories.

Q3

解析 原文只说福尔摩斯有些讨人喜欢和不讨人喜欢的习惯，但并没有比较这两者谁多谁少（outweigh）。

干扰 你可能看到有讨人喜欢和不讨人喜欢的习惯，就自行脑补主角光环觉得优点肯定大于缺点，但文章根本没提这层比较。

句子 Holmes is memorably eccentric, with a range of endearing and less endearing habits.

Q4

解析 原文确实提到了小说里苏格兰场官员被写得很平庸，但完全没提到现实中这些官员对这种描写的感受（unhappy）。

干扰 你可能觉得小说把他们写得那么笨，他们肯定不高兴，但这是你的主观推测，文章并没有交代他们的情绪态度。

句子 He is a brilliant private detective, categorically better than the plodding and mediocre officials of Scotland Yard, who constantly turn to him when they are baffled. This in itself is pure fiction: in real life there were never any brilliant private detectives to whom Scotland Yard turned when they failed, and the Yard’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) had a remarkable clear-up rate and was highly competent.

Q5

解析 原文清楚地说这纯属虚构，现实生活中根本没有苏格兰场求助过的天才私家侦探。

干扰 你可能没看到“pure fiction”（纯属虚构）或者“never any”（根本没有），从而误以为小说是有真实原型的。

句子 This in itself is pure fiction: in real life there were never any brilliant private detectives to whom Scotland Yard turned when they failed, and the Yard’s Criminal Investigation Department (CID) had a remarkable clear-up rate and was highly competent.

Q6

解析 原文说福尔摩斯故事多发生在上流社会，但现实中的犯罪其实多来自底层贫民窟和黑帮，说明小说没有反映真实情况。

干扰 你可能没有理解原文中“whereas in fact”（然而事实上）前后的对比关系，这正是说明小说和现实脱节。

句子 (C) Most of the Holmes stories are set among the higher levels of 19th-century British society, a world inhabited by professional men, retired army officers and country gentlemen, as well as members of royalty and cabinet ministers. Few take place among the working classes or the very poor, whereas in fact much crime was a product of the poverty and gangs in London’s underworld.

Q7

解析 原文说当时的女性角色通常被刻画得很单薄，只有少数（a few）女作家会写得真实些，而不是题目说的“大多数作家”（most writers）。

干扰 你可能只看到了后半句说有女性角色被写得真实，却忽略了前半句是在说刻画得“simplistic”（单一），且修饰词是“a few”而不是“most”。

句子 So, too, do the stock characters and unstated prejudices in these works: country folk and domestic servants were almost always depicted as unintelligent, and women were often depicted in a simplistic, two-dimensional way, although a few female detective writers would present female characters in a more realistic manner.

Q8

解析 原文说“除了（Apart from）”像阿加莎·克里斯蒂这样的少数巨星外，其他作家的报酬才很少（几百英镑），说明阿加莎赚的绝不止几百英镑。

干扰 你可能看到“Agatha Christie”和“a few hundred pounds”在一句话里就直接选了True，但忽略了句首的“Apart from”（除了）。

句子 Apart from a few superstars such as Agatha Christie, financial rewards for these interwar authors were rather meagre; a few hundred pounds per book—a useful income, but nothing princely.

Q9

解析 原文提到这两位美国作家的书大多是对英国模式的模仿（imitations），并且很少完全成功（seldom wholly successful）。

干扰 你可能找对了句子但填了models，但题目是说他们“不成功的（什么）”，结合原文主语，他们的书本身是不成功的模仿（imitations）。

句子 (F) US writers such as Rex Stout and Ellery Queen attempted to recreate the ‘golden age’ of British detective fiction. For the most part their books were mere imitations of the British models, although they were seldom wholly successful.

Q10

解析 原文明确提到暴力（violence）贯穿了他们两人的整个作品（appeared throughout their works）。

干扰 你可能被后面的political agenda干扰，但对应题目中“充满”（full of / throughout）这个概念的词是violence。

句子 Apart from the violence that appeared throughout their works, Hammett’s and Chandler’s novels were often marked by a political agenda that sought to expose the inequality they saw at the heart of American life.

Q11

解析 题目中的“关于社会不公的信息（message）”对应原文的“揭露美国生活核心不平等的政治（political）议程”。

干扰 词性要求是形容词修饰message，原文对应的是political修饰agenda，不能直接把名词agenda填进去。

句子 Apart from the violence that appeared throughout their works, Hammett’s and Chandler’s novels were often marked by a political agenda that sought to expose the inequality they saw at the heart of American life.

Q12

解析 原文提到像P.D. James这样的作家放弃了直白的解谜，转而写充满（full of / many）意想不到的反转（twists）的故事。

干扰 题目要求填名词复数或不可数名词，对应原文的“unexpected twists”，照抄原词即可，千万不要漏掉结尾的s。

句子 The best-known crime fiction writers, such as P. D. James, eschewed private detectives for police inspectors, and straightforward puzzles for stories that were full of unexpected twists.

Q13

解析 原文提到“科学发展总是被视为有益的（beneficial）”这种观念在传统侦探小说繁荣时期达到顶峰（言下之意现在小说没落了，社会变了，人们不再这么认为了）。

干扰 你可能不理解“reached its height during the period...”这句话的意思，其实它就是在对比过去（繁荣期大家都信科学有益）和现在（观念变了）的区别。

句子 The belief that scientific developments were invariably beneficial possibly reached its height during the period when the classic detective story flourished, as did the belief in putting rationality at the heart of Britain’s education system. And finally, the central belief that evil-doers would inevitably get their just deserts through the incorruptibility of the judicial system was replaced by a questioning of some of the procedures and decisions associated with that system.
